**DATA FLOW DIAGRAM** (Pickup & Delivery Scheduler)

**DFD Level 0 :-** *Context digram*  
![][image1]  
DFD Level 0 illustrates the overall interaction between external entities and the Pickup & Delivery Scheduler system. The system is represented as a single process to highlight how data enters and exits the system without exposing internal implementation details. Users submit pickup and delivery requests and receive order status updates. Delivery agents share availability and delivery progress while receiving task assignments from the system. The admin or monitoring system interacts with the scheduler to observe system metrics, logs, and operational reports. This level provides a high-level understanding of system boundaries and data exchange.

**DFD Level 1 – system-level Data Flow**

DFD Level 1 presents a detailed view of how data flows through the internal components of the Pickup & Delivery Scheduler system. When a user creates a pickup or delivery request, the Order Management Process validates and stores the order data in the Orders Database. An order creation event is then published to the Event Queue.

The Scheduling and Assignment Process consumes order-related events from the event queue and retrieves agent availability information from the Redis cache. Based on scheduling logic, an assignment is created and stored in the Assignments Database. A task assignment event is then published to notify the Agent Management Process.

The Agent Management Process receives assignment events, communicates task details to delivery agents, and continuously updates agent availability and delivery status. These updates are published back to the event queue and consumed by the Order Management Process to update order status in the database.The Monitoring Process collects data from all core processes to generate logs, metrics, and performance insights. These are made available to the admin or monitoring system for system observation, debugging, and performance analysis.This level clearly demonstrates the system’s event-driven nature, separation of responsibilities, and the role of databases, cache, and messaging in ensuring scalability and fault tolerance.
